title: Tensor comparisons descend through rationalization and common finite fields
statement:
Fix a prime $\ell$ and an algebraic closure $\Omega$ of $\mathbf Q_\ell$. For each finite intermediate field $E$, put $R_E=\mathcal O_E$. Let $\mathcal C_E$ be an $R_E$-linear additive symmetric monoidal category with bilinear tensor, and let $F_E:\mathcal C_E\to\operatorname{Perf}(R_E)$ be an $R_E$-linear functor, where perfect complexes mean [def-pc-perfect-ring-complex] and derived tensor products and derived scalar extensions $-\otimes^L_RN$ are those of [lem-pc-derived-tensor-second-factor-functor]. Suppose given natural isomorphisms
$$ \tau_E:F_E(X\otimes Y)\xrightarrow{\sim}F_E X\otimes^L_{R_E}F_E Y,\qquad F_E(\mathbf1)\cong R_E, $$
respecting the specified associator, symmetry and unitors. Suppose that for finite $E\subseteq L$ in $\Omega$ there are $R_E$-linear integral extension functors $T_{L/E}:\mathcal C_E\to\mathcal C_L$ ($\mathcal C_L$ regarded as $R_E$-linear through $R_E\subseteq R_L$), with natural isomorphisms $T_{E/E}\cong\operatorname{id}$ and $T_{M/L}T_{L/E}\cong T_{M/E}$ for $E\subseteq L\subseteq M$ satisfying the unit and four-field associativity equations, equipped with coherent symmetric tensor and unit comparison isomorphisms (so the transition functors are strong symmetric monoidal and their tower and identity isomorphisms are monoidal) and with natural isomorphisms $\varphi_{L/E}:F_LT_{L/E}\cong(-\otimes_{R_E}R_L)F_E$. Assume these comparisons satisfy the identity and field-tower equations and that their tensor and unit squares with $\tau_E,\tau_L$ commute, using the canonical balanced module scalar tensorator.
Form the raw rational categories $\mathcal C_E^\mathrm{rat}$ with the same objects and morphisms $\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal C_E}(X,Y)\otimes_{R_E}E$, tensor of $f\otimes a,g\otimes b$ being $(f\otimes g)\otimes ab$. Form their common-stage pair category: objects $(E,X)$ and morphisms the directed colimit of morphisms after scalar extension to common finite fields, with the given tower comparisons. These are the constructions used in [def-weil-rationalization-karoubi, def-weil-algebraically-closed-coefficients]; the target common-stage category is [def-weil-point-fd-qlbar-category].
Then $F_E^\mathrm{rat}(X)=F_EX\otimes_{R_E}E$ and $F_E^\mathrm{rat}(f\otimes a)=a(F_Ef\otimes1)$ carry a natural tensor comparison obtained from $\tau_E\otimes E$ by the balanced isomorphism $(P\otimes Q)\otimes E\cong(P\otimes E)\otimes_E(Q\otimes E)$. It has the localized unit, respects all tensor constraints, and satisfies the rational scalar tensor and unit squares.
For $(E_1,X),(E_2,Y)$ and every finite $L\supseteq E_1E_2$, the common-stage comparison is the class of $\tau_L^\mathrm{rat}$ on $T_{L/E_1}X,T_{L/E_2}Y$, composed on its target with $\varphi_{L/E_1}\otimes\varphi_{L/E_2}$ and the balanced scalar tensorator. These classes are independent of $L$ and of representatives, natural on the common-stage category, and satisfy the unit, associativity and symmetry equations. They obey the same formula at every common extension, including identity stages; their unit is the class of the rational unit from any base stage. In the common-stage formula, components written at different fields are compared through the canonical stage isomorphisms, not by literal equality of their sources. Explicitly, choose $K\supseteq E_1,E_2$ for the tensor object $U_K=T_{K/E_1}X\otimes T_{K/E_2}Y$. At $L\supseteq K$, first use $\varphi_{L/K,U_K}:F_L T_{L/K}U_K\xrightarrow{\sim} B_{L/K}F_KU_K$, in the inverse direction, and then $F_L(d_{L,K})$, where $d_{L,K}:T_{L/K}U_K\xrightarrow{\sim}U_L$ is the transition tensor comparison followed by the two tower comparisons. Here $B_{L/K}=-\otimes_K L$ and all the functors and comparisons in this formula are rationalized. If $L$ does not contain a chosen $K$, compare at any further common extension of $K,L$.

proof.text: Put $B_{S/R}=-\otimes_R^LS$. Apply [lem-sf-perfect-scalar-tensor-coherence] to $R_E\to E$, to $R_E\to R_L$, and to the resulting rational ring squares. This supplies the balanced tensorators, their units and their monoidal tower comparisons on the perfect-module targets. In particular $B_{E/R_E}F_E$ takes values in perfect $E$-complexes. A bounded finite-projective complex over a field has bounded finite-dimensional cohomology, since kernels and quotients of finite-dimensional spaces are finite-dimensional; hence it is an object of the target stages in [def-weil-point-fd-qlbar-category].

proof.text: The scalar extension of a bilinear map in [def-weil-module-base-change] applies to the composition pairings and the tensor pairings on Hom modules. Thus the displayed rational composition and tensor are well defined. Their identity and interchange equations hold on pure tensors: a composite of $(f\otimes a)$ and $(g\otimes b)$ has coefficient $ab$, and both sides of tensor interchange have coefficient $abcd$. Additivity gives the equations on finite sums. Associators, symmetries and unitors are their original components tensored with $1$; their naturality is checked in the same way on pure morphisms, and their coherence diagrams are the images of the original diagrams. This constructs the rational monoidal categories without adding any objects or idempotents.

source.place: Final paragraph: rationalization and the common-stage coefficient construction; the following explicit conditional argument is agent-written.

proof.text: The rule $f\otimes a\mapsto aB_{E/R_E}(F_Ef)$ is balanced: replacing $(rf)\otimes a$ by $f\otimes ra$ gives the same map because $F_E$ and $B_{E/R_E}$ are $R_E$-linear. The tensor-module universal property gives a map on each rational Hom module. It preserves identity and composition, since $abB(F_Eg\circ F_Ef)=(bB(F_Eg))\circ(aB(F_Ef))$. Thus it defines the functor $F_E^{\rm rat}$ with exactly the object and morphism formulas in the statement.

source.place: Final paragraph: rationalization and the common-stage coefficient construction; the following explicit conditional argument is agent-written.

proof.text: Define $\tau_E^{\rm rat}=b_{E/R_E}\circ B_{E/R_E}(\tau_E)$ and the unit by $B(F_E\mathbf1)\cong B(R_E)\cong E$. Each component is invertible. For integral $f,g$, the naturality square is the scalar extension of the assumed square for $\tau_E$, followed by the naturality square for $b$. For $f\otimes a,g\otimes b$, both paths are $ab$ times these same paths; expand finite sums to obtain full naturality. The associativity diagram is the integral diagram followed by the associativity diagram for $b$; the symmetry diagram is the integral diagram followed by the signed symmetry diagram for $b$. The two unit diagrams follow by the same composition with the multiplication unit of $B$. All these scalar diagrams are equations supplied by [lem-sf-perfect-scalar-tensor-coherence].

source.place: Final paragraph: rationalization and the common-stage coefficient construction; the following explicit conditional argument is agent-written.

proof.text: Extend $T_{L/E}$ on morphisms by $f\otimes a\mapsto T_{L/E}(f)\otimes a$, using $E\subseteq L$. This is balanced by $R_E$-linearity. Extend every comparison by its integral component tensored with $1$. Naturality on fractions follows by multiplication by the scalar, as in the preceding step. Each identity, tower, tensor or unit equation is an equality between composites of those components, hence remains an equality after scalar extension. On the module side identify $(P\otimes_{R_E}R_L)\otimes_{R_L}L$ with $(P\otimes_{R_E}E)\otimes_E L$: both are represented by $P\otimes_{R_E}L$ and $(x\otimes a)\otimes b\mapsto x\otimes ab$. The tower and tensor compatibility of these identifications is [lem-sf-perfect-scalar-tensor-coherence]. This gives $\varphi^{\rm rat}_{L/E}:F_L^{\rm rat}T_{L/E}^{\rm rat}\cong B_{L/E}F_E^{\rm rat}$ and precisely the rational scalar tensor and unit squares.

source.place: Final paragraph: rationalization and the common-stage coefficient construction; the following explicit conditional argument is agent-written.

proof.text: For the remainder write $F,T,\varphi$ for the rational data. Let $c^C$ denote the transition tower isomorphisms and $c^D$ the module scalar tower isomorphisms. Define the common-stage functor on objects by $(E,X)\mapsto(E,F_EX)$. For $[L,u]:(E,X)\to(E',Y)$ use the representative $v_L=\varphi_{L/E',Y}\,F_L(u)\,\varphi_{L/E,X}^{-1}$. At $M\supseteq L$ source transport is $u_M=c^C_{M/L/E'}T_{M/L}(u)(c^C_{M/L/E})^{-1}$. Substitute this into $v_M$, apply naturality of $\varphi_{M/L}$ to $u$, and use its tower equation on the two ends. The result is $v_M=c^D_{M/L/E'}B_{M/L}(v_L)(c^D_{M/L/E})^{-1}$. This is exactly the target transition of [def-weil-point-fd-qlbar-category], after the following identification, used also in steps 7--11. Over a field every complex is K-flat, so by [lem-pc-derived-tensor-second-factor-functor](2) the derived extension $B_{M/L}$ is canonically the termwise extension $T_{M/L}$ used in that definition; on a complex $C$ the helper's $c^D_{M/L/E}$ is then represented by $(x\otimes s)\otimes t\mapsto x\otimes st$, which is the termwise map characterizing $c_{M/L/E}$ in [lem-weil-derived-field-scalar-extension-tower](2), and likewise for the unit maps by (1). So $c^D$ and the definition's $c$ coincide. Therefore equivalent representatives give equal classes. Composition and addition are preserved at a common stage because $\varphi^{-1}\varphi$ cancels, while identities follow from the unit equation even when $T_{E/E}$ is merely isomorphic to the identity.

proof.text: For a pair of objects choose $K\supseteq E_1,E_2$ and $U_K=T_{K/E_1}X\otimes T_{K/E_2}Y$. For $L\supseteq K$ put $d_{L,K}=(c^C_{L/K/E_1}\otimes c^C_{L/K/E_2})\,t_{L/K}$, with $t$ the strong transition tensor comparison. This identifies $T_{L/K}U_K$ with $U_L$. The monoidality of $c^C$ and its four-field equation give $d_{M,L}T_{M/L}(d_{L,K})=d_{M,K}c^C_{M/L/K}$. The target has the corresponding maps $e_{L,K}:B_{L/K}V_K\to V_L$, where $V_K=B_{K/E_1}F_{E_1}X\otimes B_{K/E_2}F_{E_2}Y$; its analogous equation follows from [lem-sf-perfect-scalar-tensor-coherence]. For morphism pairs define their tensor after extension to a common stage, conjugating by $d$; functoriality and the displayed equation show that further transport gives the same class. Equality of different representatives is tested at a common larger field as in [def-weil-algebraically-closed-coefficients]. The same equations show that tensor objects chosen at different fields are canonically isomorphic. Represent the associator and symmetry by the stage associator and symmetry at one field, conjugated by these tensor-stage identifications. Take the unit at $\mathbf Q_\ell$; represent its unitors after the transition unit identification. Monoidality of transition functors makes these components compatible with further extension and natural on represented arrows. The pentagon, hexagon and triangle diagrams are finite diagrams: choose a field containing their finitely many chosen stages, cancel $d$ and the tower maps on adjacent edges, and they become the corresponding stage diagrams. Thus these prescriptions give the monoidal constraints used below.

source.place: Final paragraph: rationalization and the common-stage coefficient construction; the following explicit conditional argument is agent-written.

proof.text:
Set $\gamma_K=(\varphi_{K/E_1}\otimes\varphi_{K/E_2})\tau_{K,T_{K/E_1}X,T_{K/E_2}Y}:F_KU_K\to V_K$. The rational scalar tensor square of step 5, evaluated on the two transported objects at $K$, and the tower equations for $\varphi$ give
$$\gamma_L F_L(d_{L,K})\varphi_{L/K,U_K}^{-1}=e_{L,K}B_{L/K}(\gamma_K).$$
Indeed expand the left side: move $F_L(t_{L/K})$ across $\tau_L$ by the scalar tensor square; move $F_L(c^C)$ across $\varphi$ by the tower equation for each factor; the two remaining scalar tensorators compose to $e_{L,K}$ by [lem-sf-perfect-scalar-tensor-coherence]. Thus $\gamma_L$, after the required source and target identifications, represents precisely the transition of $\gamma_K$. For two incomparable common fields take their compositum and apply the equality twice. This proves independence of the common field and the formula at every common extension, with the source transport specified in the corrected statement.

source.place: Final paragraph: rationalization and the common-stage coefficient construction; the following explicit conditional argument is agent-written.

proof.text: Take morphisms between each of the two input objects, and representatives for both morphisms over one common field $L$. Identify all four input objects at $L$ using the tower maps. Naturality of $\tau_L$ and of the two $\varphi$ gives the naturality square for $\gamma_L$. The common-stage functor and tensor of arrows were defined by these very conjugations in steps 6 and 7, so the square is the desired square of classes. Replacing representatives by equal ones amounts to extending to a stage where the two input arrows are equal, and the equation of step 8 identifies the resulting components there. No full faithfulness of $F$ or any transition functor is used.

source.place: Final paragraph: rationalization and the common-stage coefficient construction; the following explicit conditional argument is agent-written.

proof.text: Choose the common-stage unit at the base field $\mathbf Q_\ell$. The unit comparisons of $T$ and the tower isomorphisms identify its extension to each finite field with that field's unit. The module scalar-unit comparisons do the same on the target. The rational scalar unit square from step 5 then identifies the class of the base unit component with the component from every other base stage. Its inverse is represented by the inverse rational unit component. All equal-field identifications use the given identity isomorphisms; their naturality cancels them, rather than identifying $T_{E/E}$ literally with the identity.

source.place: Final paragraph: rationalization and the common-stage coefficient construction; the following explicit conditional argument is agent-written.

proof.text: For three objects choose a single field containing their fields and all fields chosen for the intermediate tensors. Under $d$ and $e$, both iterated common-stage comparisons are the two paths of the associativity diagram for $\tau_L$ and $\varphi$ at that field. Step 8 permits these replacements without changing either class. That rational diagram commutes by steps 4 and 5, and its scalar reassociations commute by [lem-sf-perfect-scalar-tensor-coherence]. For two objects the same procedure gives the symmetry diagram at one field, including its Koszul sign. For either unitor it gives the rational unitor diagram, using the unit identification of step 10. Thus associativity, symmetry and both unit equations hold in the common-stage category. Each comparison is an isomorphism since its representative is an isomorphism and its inverse has the compatible transitions. This proves all the claimed clauses.
